body:
Reviews of #1746 + #1866 (Joe asked me to review both and feed back).

#1746 (TASK-1205, codex-authored — INDEPENDENT review): design is SOUND and matches acceptance (report-only cross-target check, portability ratchet, path-filtered xplat trigger, Windows-safe git_ops fixture). But I read the actual failing steps, and the red is NOT conclusively real:
- ubuntu Build FAIL = the new cross-target step: "failed to run custom build command for ring v0.17.14 / cc-rs: failed to find tool lib.exe" — i.e. cross-compiling ring (C dep) for windows-msvc on the Linux runner, the EXACT limitation the PR's own CLAUDE.md note documents. That step is `continue-on-error: true` in the diff, so it should fail-SOFT. The job failing anyway means either the run (2026-09-12, 111 commits stale) predates continue-on-error, OR the flag's scoping isn't taking effect. That's the one thing to verify.
- windows Build FAIL: the log shows all tests passing (ok), failing step unclear — inconclusive.
Verdict: NOT mergeable as-is, but the fix is likely just staleness. Decisive next step: rebase onto current main + fresh CI. If green → operator-reviewed CI-change merge (stays escalated to Joe, it modifies CI). If ubuntu red persists → the continue-on-error scoping is the real bug (the report-only step must never fail the job). Also confirm the windows failing step. Sibling #1775 already landed part of TASK-1205, so #1746 is the remaining CI-guard slice.

#1866 (BUG-1173, MINE — author confirming your review, NOT a merge vote): I VERIFIED your self-shelve claim in the code. `grep -rn 'merge-hold-gate' --include=*.rs` = ZERO hits in the CI-watch/auto_complete path; only doc-comments in merge_hold.rs. So phase-2 CI-watch has no exclusion — a red merge-hold-gate IS treated as a failed required check → shelve. Your RequestChanges is correct and code-confirmed. #1866's own green CI does NOT refute it: the label is applied at RUNTIME during a drive drain (set_pr_number → sync_label(true)), not statically on #1866's PR, so the self-shelve only fires when a drive spec actually drains. Static green != safe.
Fix: your "keep write_hold at PR-detection, defer sync_label to record_merge_supervision_hold (post-CI)" is the right minimal close. Alternative worth noting: teach phase-2 CI-watch to treat merge-hold-gate as a known-non-blocking check (exclude from the shelve decision) — more robust long-term (survives a lingering label) but a bigger change; defer-label is the right scope for BUG-1173's residual. Either way needs a non-mock GitHub-loop regression test. I'll take the keyboard fix on #1866; it stays open + un-merged.
